data.title: Semaglutide Versus Empagliflozin in Uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes: A Cohort Study With 18 Months of Follow-Up (SEMPA18).
data.abstract:
INTRODUCTION
Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic disease that substantially increases morbidity and mortality through its cardiovascular and renal complications. Beyond mere glycemic control, current guidelines from the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) and Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) recommend interventions that confer additional cardiovascular and renal benefits.
OBJECTIVE
This study aims to assess and compare the efficacy of semaglutide versus empagliflozin in improving glycemic control, weight, blood pressure, and renal function in patients with uncontrolled T2DM after 18 months of follow-up.
METHODS
This retrospective cohort study included 41 patients with uncontrolled T2DM (glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) > 7%) who received either empagliflozin (n=20) or semaglutide (n=21) as monotherapy. Clinical and laboratory parameters (HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, body weight, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, serum creatinine, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and urine microalbumin) were measured at baseline and 18 months (SEMPA18). Changes were compared between the two groups using appropriate statistical methods.
RESULTS
Of the 41 participants (58.5% male), 20 were treated with empagliflozin and 21 with semaglutide. After 18 months, median HbA1c decreased from 7.60% to 6.85% in the empagliflozin group (100% improved) and from 7.90% to 7.00% in the semaglutide group (95.2% improved). A reduction in body weight of 5% or more was achieved by 2 of 20 (10.0%) empagliflozin-treated patients versus 6 of 21 (28.6%) among those on semaglutide (p=0.48). Albuminuria improved in 18 of 20 (90.0%) empagliflozin users (median final: 12.0 mg/dL) compared to 14 of 21 (66.7%) semaglutide users (median final: 20.0 mg/dL), although the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.07). Both groups showed gains in eGFR (final median: 80.50 vs. 71.00 mL/min/1.73 m²; p=0.048), and serum creatinine decreased in the majority of patients (75.0% vs. 71.4%). A subgroup analysis revealed that heart failure status (LVEF < 50% or documented diagnosis) was associated with less improvement in renal markers, particularly serum creatinine, regardless of the treatment group.
CONCLUSIONS
In this real-world, 18-month cohort, empagliflozin produced more pronounced improvements in albuminuria and a slightly greater absolute reduction in HbA1c, whereas semaglutide showed a trend toward greater weight loss, though not statistically significant. These findings emphasize individualized therapy choices in T2DM based on cardiorenal risk profiles and underscore the potential value of early empagliflozin initiation, especially in patients at higher risk of renal deterioration.

data.title: Renal and Cardiovascular Outcomes After Weight Loss From Gastric Bypass Surgery in Type 2 Diabetes: Cardiorenal Risk Reductions Exceed Atherosclerotic Benefits.
data.abstract:
OBJECTIVE
We examined detailed renal and cardiovascular (CV) outcomes after gastric bypass (GBP) surgery in people with obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), across several renal function categories, in a nationwide cohort study.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
We linked data from the National Diabetes Register and the Scandinavian Obesity Surgery Register with four national databases holding information on socioeconomic variables, medications, hospitalizations, and causes of death and matched 5,321 individuals with T2DM who had undergone GBP with 5,321 who had not (age 18-65 years, mean BMI >40 kg/m 2 , mean follow-up >4.5 years). The risks of postoperative outcomes were assessed with Cox regression models.
RESULTS
During the first years postsurgery, there were small reductions in creatinine and albuminuria and stable estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in the GBP group. The incidence rates of most outcomes relating to renal function, CV disease, and mortality were lower after GBP, being particularly marked for heart failure (hazard ratio [HR] 0.33 [95% CI 0.24, 0.46]) and CV mortality (HR 0.36 [(95% CI 0.22, 0.58]). The risk of a composite of severe renal disease or halved eGFR was 0.56 (95% CI 0.44, 0.71), whereas nonfatal CV risk was lowered less (HR 0.82 [95% CI 0.70, 0.97]) after GBP. Risks for key outcomes were generally lower after GBP in all eGFR strata, including in individuals with eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m 2 .
CONCLUSIONS
Our data suggest robust benefits for renal outcomes, heart failure, and CV mortality after GBP in individuals with obesity and T2DM. These results suggest that marked weight loss yields important benefits, particularly on the cardiorenal axis (including slowing progression to end-stage renal disease), whatever the baseline renal function status.

data.title: Kidney function measures and cardiovascular outcomes in people with diabetes: the Hoorn Diabetes Care System cohort.
data.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS
Both manifestations of kidney disease in diabetes, reduced eGFR (ml/min per 1.73 m 2 ) and increased urinary albumin/creatinine ratio (UACR, mg/mmol), may increase the risk of specific CVD subtypes in adults with diabetes.
METHODS
We assessed the prospective association between annually recorded measures of eGFR and UACR and the occurrence of myocardial infarction (MI), CHD, stroke, heart failure (HF) and cardiovascular mortality in 13,657 individuals with diabetes (53.6% male, age 62.3±12.1 years) from the Hoorn Diabetes Care System cohort, using data obtained between 1998 and 2018. Multivariate time-dependent Cox regression models adjusted for cardiovascular risk factors were used to estimate HRs and 95% CI. Associations of eGFR were adjusted for UACR values and vice versa. Effect modification by sex was investigated for all associations.
RESULTS
After a mean follow-up period of 7 years, event rates per 1000 person-years were 3.08 for MI, 3.72 for CHD, 1.12 for HF, 0.84 for stroke and 6.25 for cardiovascular mortality. Mildly reduced eGFR (60-90 ml/min per 1.73 m 2 ) and moderately to severely reduced eGFR (<59 ml/min per 1.73 m 2 ) were associated with higher risks of MI (HR 1.52; 95% CI 1.10, 2.12 and HR 1.69; 95% CI 1.09, 2.64) and CHD (HR 1.67; 95% CI 1.23, 2.26 and HR 2.01; 95% CI 1.34, 3.02) compared with normal eGFR (>90 ml/min per 1.73 m 2 ). Mildly reduced eGFR was associated with a higher risk of stroke (HR 2.53; 95% CI 1.27, 5.03). Moderately increased UACR (3-30 mg/mmol) and severely increased UACR (>30 mg/mmol) were prospectively associated with a higher cardiovascular mortality risk in men and women (HR 1.87; 95% CI 1.41, 2.47 and HR 2.78; 95% CI 1.78, 4.34) compared with normal UACR (<3 mg/mmol). Significant effect modification by sex was observed for the association between UACR and HF. Because there were a limited number of HF events within the category of UACR >30 mg/mmol, categories were combined into UACR <3.0 and >3.0 mg/mmol in the stratified analysis. Women but not men with UACR >3.0 mg/mmol had a significantly higher risk of HF compared with normal UACR (HR 2.79; 95% CI 1.47, 5.28).
CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION
This study showed differential and independent prospective associations between manifestations of early kidney damage in diabetes and several CVD subtypes, suggesting that regular monitoring of both kidney function measures may help to identify individuals at higher risk of specific cardiovascular events.

trajectory.final_answer:
# Summary

Baseline albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in type 2 diabetes independently predict future heart failure hospitalization and cardiovascular mortality, with higher risk generally observed when albuminuria is present—alone or combined with reduced eGFR—and with greater risk as kidney dysfunction worsens. Large cohorts and meta-analyses show graded risks for heart failure and cardiovascular death across categories of albuminuria and eGFR, and suggest that both measures add prognostic information beyond traditional risk factors. These markers also inform treatment selection, as SGLT2 inhibitors reduce cardiorenal outcomes across a broad range of baseline albuminuria and eGFR, including below previously emphasized thresholds.

# Baseline Albuminuria and Future Heart Failure

Prospective cohort data indicate that albuminuria, whether isolated or accompanied by reduced eGFR, is associated with higher risks of heart failure hospitalization in type 2 diabetes. In the Hong Kong Diabetes Biobank (n≈19,000; median follow-up ≈54,000 person-years), participants with decreased eGFR without albuminuria had a 3.08-fold higher hazard of heart failure hospitalization versus those without DKD (95% CI 1.82–5.21), and risks were even higher in the presence of albuminuria with or without reduced eGFR, reflecting a cumulative adverse effect of kidney injury phenotypes on cardiorenal outcomes. <cite id="34999159">Compared with the no-DKD subgroup, the subgroup with decreased eGFR without albuminuria had higher risks of hospitalization for heart failure (HR 3.08 [95% CI 1.82–5.21]); the risks of hospitalization for HF were higher in the setting of albuminuria with or without decreased eGFR</cite>.

Albuminuria also shows graded associations with incident heart failure in diabetes cohorts beyond DKD. In the Hong Kong Diabetes Register (n=2,139), higher circulating branched-chain amino acids tracked with incident heart failure and adjusted hazard ratios remained significant across increasing albuminuria categories, including after adjustment for coronary events, lipids, glycemia, and kidney function, underscoring albuminuria as an independent risk marker for HF. <cite id="31957226">Serum BCAAs had a positive linear association with incident HF (per-SD increase HR 1.22 [95% CI 1.07–1.39]); the HR remained significant after adjustment including albuminuria and eGFR</cite>.

Mechanistically and clinically, albuminuria reflects endothelial injury and extracellular matrix accumulation and is linked to cardiorenal risk across sexes and albuminuria severities. In a large Japanese cohort (n=4,328), men with microalbuminuria had substantially higher risks of ESKD than women, and moderately increased albuminuria showed strong sex differences in ESKD risk, highlighting that albuminuria severity modifies cardiorenal outcomes. <cite id="36785912">Among patients with microalbuminuria, men had a substantially higher risk of ESKD versus women; incidence rates were increased in men versus women with albuminuria around 300 mg/g</cite>.

# Baseline eGFR and Cardiovascular Mortality

Lower baseline eGFR is associated with increased cardiovascular mortality in type 2 diabetes, with risks rising as kidney function declines. In the Hoorn Diabetes Care System cohort (n=13,657; median follow-up 7 years), mildly reduced eGFR (60–90 mL/min/1.73 m²) and more severe reduction (<59 mL/min/1.73 m²) predicted higher risks of myocardial infarction, coronary heart disease, and stroke, and mildly reduced eGFR was linked to higher stroke risk; importantly, cardiovascular mortality risk increased with higher urinary albumin/creatinine categories in both sexes. <cite id="36347992">Mildly reduced eGFR (60–90 ml/min per 1.73 m²) and moderately to severely reduced eGFR (<59 ml/min per 1.73 m²) were associated with higher risks of MI and CHD; moderately increased UACR (3–30 mg/mmol) and severely increased UACR (>30 mg/mmol) were associated with higher cardiovascular mortality risk in men and women</cite>.

These associations persist when comparing individuals with and without diabetes, indicating an excess cardiovascular risk that is modified by kidney function. In a nationwide matched cohort of 5,321 patients with T2DM and 5,321 controls (mean BMI >40 kg/m²; mean follow-up >4.5 years), Roukova et al. observed particularly marked reductions in heart failure and cardiovascular mortality after gastric bypass, with benefits evident across all eGFR strata, including eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m², underscoring that baseline renal impairment does not negate the prognostic impact of kidney dysfunction on CV outcomes. <cite id="32152136">The incidence rates of heart failure and CV mortality were lower after GBP, being particularly marked for heart failure (HR 0.33 [95% CI 0.24, 0.46]) and CV mortality (HR 0.36 [95% CI 0.22, 0.58]); risks for key outcomes were generally lower after GBP in all eGFR strata, including individuals with eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²</cite>.

# Combined Albuminuria and eGFR: Differential and Independent Associations

Multiple cohorts suggest that albuminuria and reduced eGFR track different, yet complementary, pathways of vascular and renal injury, with distinct associations to specific cardiovascular events. In Diabetologia's Hoorn cohort, reduced eGFR more strongly predicted atherosclerotic events (MI, CHD), whereas increased UACR was more closely tied to stroke and cardiovascular mortality, with notable sex-specific effects for HF risk in women with higher UACR. <cite id="36347992">Mildly reduced eGFR was associated with higher MI, CHD, and stroke risks; moderately to severely increased UACR was associated with higher cardiovascular mortality; significant effect modification by sex was observed for the association between UACR and HF, with women but not men with UACR >3.0 mg/mmol having higher HF risk</cite>.

# Clinical Implications and Treatment

Baseline albuminuria and eGFR not only predict risk but also guide therapy. SGLT2 inhibitors reduce kidney and cardiovascular outcomes across heart failure, CKD, and type 2 diabetes, including in patients with albuminuria at or below commonly used thresholds (e.g., UACR ≥30 mg/mmol). A recent meta-analysis and pooled data show ≈36–41% relative risk reductions for composite kidney outcomes and consistent benefits across subpopulations, including those with lower baseline albuminuria and eGFR, supporting broader use of SGLT2 inhibitors to mitigate cardiorenal risk in T2DM. <cite id="39230974">SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the risk of the composite kidney end point by 41% in heart failure, 36% in CKD, and 38% in type 2 diabetes; a similar pattern of benefit was observed across combinations of comorbidities and in patients without baseline heart failure, CKD, or T2DM</cite>. <cite id="39230974,41206830">Consistent effects on kidney outcomes were observed in most subpopulations; a model-based approach integrating CKD risk scores with treatment effects suggests targeting SGLT2 inhibitors can identify patients with uACR <3 mg/mmol who derive greater absolute benefit than those with higher uACR</cite>.

# Practical Takeaways

- Albuminuria at baseline—regardless of eGFR category—confers higher risk of heart failure hospitalization and cardiovascular mortality in type 2 diabetes, with additive risk when combined with reduced eGFR. <cite id="34999159">The risks of death, CVD, hospitalization for HF, and CKD progression were higher in the setting of albuminuria with or without decreased eGFR</cite>.
- Lower eGFR is associated with increased atherosclerotic and cardiovascular mortality, with risks rising progressively as kidney function declines. <cite id="36347992">Mildly reduced eGFR and more severe reductions were associated with higher MI, CHD, and stroke risks; cardiovascular mortality increased with higher UACR categories</cite>.
- Both albuminuria and eGFR independently and differentially predict specific cardiovascular events, with implications for monitoring and sex-specific risk stratification. <cite id="36347992">Reduced eGFR more strongly predicted atherosclerotic events, whereas UACR was more closely linked to stroke and cardiovascular mortality, with women showing higher HF risk at higher UACR</cite>.
- Therapeutically, SGLT2 inhibitors provide cardioprotection across a broad spectrum of baseline albuminuria and eGFR in T2DM, supporting their use even in patients with lower albuminuria or eGFR. <cite id="39230974,41206830">SGLT2 inhibitors reduced composite kidney outcomes across heart failure, CKD, and T2DM; model-based strategies can identify subgroups with uACR <3 mg/mmol who derive greater absolute benefit</cite>.

# Limitations and Considerations

Observational designs, residual confounding, and heterogeneous populations limit causal inference, and some cohorts focus on specific subgroups (e.g., obesity with T2DM). Nonetheless, consistent findings across large cohorts and meta-analyses support the prognostic and therapeutic relevance of baseline albuminuria and eGFR for future heart failure and cardiovascular mortality in type 2 diabetes. <cite id="34999159">The Hong Kong Diabetes Biobank found higher HF hospitalization and mortality risks with albuminuria phenotypes, with sensitivity analyses yielding similar findings</cite>. <cite id="36347992">The Hoorn cohort demonstrated differential and independent associations of albuminuria and eGFR with specific CVD outcomes, supporting routine monitoring of both measures</cite>.

<snippet id="37082097">Title: Treatment outcomes of mucosal melanoma of head and neck: Efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors for advanced disease.
Authors: Ohshima, Shusuke, Ueki, Yushi, Yokoyama, Yusuke et al. | Year: 2022 | Journal: Frontiers in surgery
Abstract: BACKGROUND
Head and neck mucosal melanoma (HNMM) is a rare and aggressive subtype of melanoma. HNMM often develops as a recurrent or metastatic disease, and its prognosis is worse than that of cutaneous melanoma. Recent large-scale clinical studies have reported favorable outcomes with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) for melanoma. However, these clinical trials included only a small number of HNMM cases. This study aimed to estimate treatment outcomes and prognostic predictors of ICIs for advanced HNMM.
METHODS
Cases of advanced HNMM, defined as unresectable or metastatic HNMM at the initial diagnosis (five patients) or development of recurrent/metastatic HNMM after initial treatment (27 patients), were included in this study. Survival analysis and a search for prognostic factors were performed for these 32 patients. Furthermore, the detailed clinical course of patients who received ICI treatment was investigated.
RESULTS
The median overall survival (OS) of 32 patients with advanced HNMM was 25.3 months. The estimated 1-, 3-, and 5-year OS rates were 68.4%, 42.8%, and 34.3%, respectively. Fourteen patients (43.7%) received ICIs, whereas 18 (56.3%) did not. Univariate analysis showed that ICI treatment was the only factor associated with a better 1-year OS. Patients who received ICI treatment had significantly longer OS (median OS: not reached, 1-year OS: 85.7%) than those who did not (median OS: 11.3 months, 1-year OS: 54.5%). The overall response and disease control rates of patients who received ICI treatment were 50% and 64.3%, respectively. Patients who achieved complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) to ICI treatment survived significantly longer (1-year OS: 100%) than those who did not (1-year OS: 71.4%). Among the five patients who discontinued ICI treatment due to severe immune-related adverse events (irAEs), four did not receive salvage treatments but showed durable treatment effects and survived for 9.8-54.2 months at the end of the follow-up period.
CONCLUSIONS
ICI treatment achieved a favorable OS for advanced HNMM. CR/PR to ICI treatment and discontinuation owing to severe irAEs were favorable predictors of OS.</snippet>

- In a series of advanced head‑and‑neck mucosal melanoma, five patients discontinued PD‑1/PD‑L1 therapy due to severe irAEs. <snippet id="28239466">Title: Nivolumab induced myxedema crisis.
Authors: Khan, Uqba, Rizvi, Humaira, Sano, Dahlia et al. | Year: 2017 | Journal: Journal for immunotherapy of cancer
Abstract: BACKGROUND
Nivolumab is an anti-programmed cell death (anti-PD-1) monoclonal antibody that is approved by Food and Drug Administration for treatment of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, metastatic melanoma, relapsed Hodgkin lymphoma and advanced renal cell cancer. We report a rare case of myxedema crisis induced by nivolumab in a patient with metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of lung.
CASE PRESENTATION
Fifty three-year old woman with metastatic squamous cell carcinoma currently on treatment with nivolumab presented with diffuse facial and tongue swelling, slurred speech, depressed mentation, fatigue and weakness. Initial evaluation revealed severe hypothyroidism with thyroid stimulating hormone of 237 micro Unit/mL (Normal Reference range: 0.27-4.20 micro unit/mL) and undetectable free T4. Patient was diagnosed with nivolumab induced myxedema crisis. She was treated successfully with levothyroxine with complete resolution of her symptoms. Nivolumab was safely restarted once the symptoms of myxedema resolved.
CONCLUSION
Nivolumab can cause immune-mediated endocrinopathies including thyroiditis, hypophysitis, adrenal insufficiency and type 1 diabetes mellitus. High index of suspicion and periodic measurement of thyroid function tests are recommended in patients receiving nivolumab therapy. Our case also suggests that once the myxedema crisis is treated and symptoms are resolved, nivolumab can be safely re-challenged.</snippet>

Abstract: Atherosclerosis is considered an irreversible process, with crucial contribution of inflammation and immune cells. Impact of cancer immunotherapy on a partly immune-driven disease, such as atherosclerosis, is poorly understood, but preclinical models suggest its worsening on programmed death/ligand-1 (PD-1/PD-L1) inhibitors. In a previously reported cohort of 11 patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treated with nivolumab and pre-existing complicated atheromatous plaques, 3 patients had a dramatic radiologic reduction of aortic plaques while on nivolumab; of these 3, 2 died receiving no further treatment. The remaining patient was an 83-year-old woman with history of arterial hypertension and hypothyroidism who was diagnosed with locally advanced squamous NSCLC. At relapse, complicated aortic atheromatous plaques were demonstrated on scans. The patient was then treated with nivolumab obtaining stable disease at radiological assessment, which also demonstrated almost complete vanishing of aortic plaques. After relapse and interval treatment with chemotherapy, she experienced new development of aortic atheromatous plaques. At further relapse she received atezolizumab, which yielded disease response and new reduction in aortic plaques, until nearly complete resolution. The observation of a repeated improvement of atheromatous plaques on treatment with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors favors the protective role of T cells on atheromatous plaques that is impaired by PD-L1 expression by plaque-associated macrophages. Validation by independent and prospective observation is needed.</snippet>

<snippet id="34646270">Title: Safety and Efficacy of the Rechallenge of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors After Immune-Related Adverse Events in Patients With Cancer: A Systemic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Authors: Zhao, Qing, Zhang, Jianwei, Xu, Lingyi et al. | Year: 2021 | Journal: Frontiers in immunology
Abstract: INTRODUCTION
Little evidence exists on the safety and efficacy of the rechallenge of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) after immune-related adverse events (irAEs) in patients with cancer.
METHODS
We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane for articles on ICI rechallenge after irAEs for systemic review and meta-analysis. The outcomes included the incidence and associated factors for safety and objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) for efficacy.
RESULTS
A total of 789 ICI rechallenge cases from 18 cohort studies, 5 case series studies, and 54 case reports were included. The pooled incidence of all-grade and high-grade irAEs after rechallenge in patients with cancer was 34.2% and 11.7%, respectively. Compared with initial ICI treatment, rechallenge showed a higher incidence for all-grade irAEs (OR, 3.81; 95% CI, 2.15-6.74; p < 0.0001), but similar incidence for high-grade irAEs ( p > 0.05). Types of initial irAEs (pneumonitis and global irAEs) and cancer (non-small cell lung cancer and multiple cancer) recapitulated these findings. Gastrointestinal irAEs and time interval between initial irAEs and ICI rechallenge were associated with higher recurrence of high-grade irAEs ( p < 0.05), whereas initial anti-PD-1/PD-L1 antibodies were associated with a lower recurrence ( p < 0.05). Anti-PD-1/PD-L1 antibodies rechallenge was associated with a lower all-grade irAE recurrence ( p < 0.05). The pooled ORR and DCR after rechallenge were 43.1% and 71.9%, respectively, showing no significant difference compared with initial ICI treatment ( p > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS
ICI rechallenge after irAEs showed lower safety and similar efficacy outcomes compared with initial ICI treatment.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION
PROSPERO, identifier CRD42020191405.</snippet>

Authors: Hwang, Soo Young, Hsieh, Pinghsin, Zhang, Wei | Year: 2024 | Journal: Hepatology communications
Abstract: BACKGROUND
In recent years, the use of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) has become a cornerstone in cancer treatment. METHODS
PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL databases were searched in July 2023 based on keywords including ICIs (anti-Programmed cell death protein 1/Programmed Death-Ligand 1, anti-CTLA-4, and anti-LAG3) and hepatitis.

<snippet id="28239462">Title: Thrombocytopenia in patients with melanoma receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
Authors: Shiuan, Eileen, Beckermann, Kathryn E, Ozgun, Alpaslan et al. | Year: 2017 | Journal: Journal for immunotherapy of cancer
Abstract: BACKGROUND
Immune checkpoint inhibitors, including antibodies against programmed death 1 (PD-1) and cytotoxic T-lymphocyte antigen 4 (CTLA-4), are being used with increasing frequency for the treatment of cancer. Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) including colitis, dermatitis, and pneumonitis are well described, but less frequent events are now emerging with larger numbers of patients treated. Herein we describe the incidence and spectrum of thrombocytopenia following immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy and two severe cases of idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP).
CASE PRESENTATIONS
A 47-year-old female with recurrent BRAF mutant positive melanoma received combination anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4. Two weeks later, she presented with mucosal bleeding, petechiae, and thrombocytopenia and was treated with standard therapy for ITP with steroids and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Her diagnosis was confirmed with bone marrow biopsy, and given the lack of treatment response, she was treated with rituximab. She began to have recovery and stabilization of her platelet count that ultimately allowed her to be retreated with PD-1 inhibition with no further thrombocytopenia. A second patient, a 45-year-old female with a BRAF wild-type melanoma, received anti-PD-1 monotherapy and became thrombocytopenic 43 days later. Three weeks of steroid treatment improved her platelet count, but thrombocytopenia recurred and required additional steroids. She later received anti-CTLA-4 monotherapy and developed severe ITP with intracranial hemorrhage. Her ITP resolved after treatment of prednisone, IVIG, and rituximab and discontinuation of checkpoint inhibition. In a retrospective chart review of 2360 patients with melanoma treated with checkpoint inhibitor therapy, <1% experienced thrombocytopenia following immune checkpoint inhibition, and of these, most had spontaneous resolution and did not require treatment.
CONCLUSIONS
Thrombocytopenia, especially ITP, induced by immune checkpoint inhibitors appears to be an uncommon irAE that is manageable with observation in mild cases and/or standard ITP treatment algorithms. In our series, the majority of patients had mild thrombocytopenia that resolved spontaneously or responded to standard corticosteroid regimens. However, in two severe cases, IVIG and rituximab, in addition to steroids, were required. Checkpoint inhibition was resumed successfully in the first patient but rechallenge was not tolerated by the second patient.</snippet>

# Bottom line

- There is growing clinical evidence—mainly case reports and small case series—that immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can be rechallenged after immune-related adverse events (irAEs), with successful tumor control in selected patients, but rechallenge carries a higher risk of irAE recurrence, particularly for organ-specific toxicities, and requires careful patient selection and monitoring. <cite id="34646270,35389138,39225744">There is growing clinical evidence—mainly case reports and small case series—that immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can be rechallenged after immune-related adverse events (irAEs), with successful tumor control in selected patients, but rechallenge carries a higher risk of irAE recurrence, particularly for organ-specific toxicities, and requires careful patient selection and monitoring.</cite>

# What supports re-challenge?

- Systematic reviews and meta-analyses have synthesized outcomes across many rechallenge cases. One meta-analysis of 789 rechallenges from 18 cohort and case series studies found that rechallenge was feasible but not without risk, with pooled all-grade and high-grade irAE recurrence rates of 34.2% and 11.7%, respectively, and noted that certain irAE types (e.g., pneumonitis, global irAEs) and tumor types (e.g., NSCLC) were associated with higher recurrence. <cite id="34646270">A meta-analysis of 789 rechallenges from 18 cohort and case series studies found that rechallenge was feasible but not without risk, with pooled all-grade and high-grade irAE recurrence rates of 34.2% and 11.7%, respectively, and noted that certain irAE types (e.g., pneumonitis, global irAEs) and tumor types (e.g., NSCLC) were associated with higher recurrence.</cite>

- Disease-specific and organ-specific case series provide concrete examples. - Rechallenge appears feasible and sometimes beneficial for selected patients, particularly when irAEs are steroid-responsive and not organ-limiting, and when careful monitoring and risk mitigation are in place. <cite id="35389138">Rechallenge appears feasible and sometimes beneficial for selected patients, particularly when irAEs are steroid-responsive and not organ-limiting, and when careful monitoring and risk mitigation are in place.</cite> Evidence suggests that anti–PD-1/PD-L1 rechallenge may carry a lower risk of overall irAE recurrence compared with CTLA-4–related rechallenge, and that longer time intervals from initial irAE to rechallenge may reduce high-grade toxicity recurrence. <cite id="34646270">Evidence suggests that anti–PD-1/PD-L1 rechallenge may carry a lower risk of overall irAE recurrence compared with CTLA-4–related rechallenge, and that longer time intervals from initial irAE to rechallenge may reduce high-grade toxicity recurrence.</cite>

data.title: Nivolumab induced myxedema crisis.
data.abstract:
BACKGROUND
Nivolumab is an anti-programmed cell death (anti-PD-1) monoclonal antibody that is approved by Food and Drug Administration for treatment of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, metastatic melanoma, relapsed Hodgkin lymphoma and advanced renal cell cancer. We report a rare case of myxedema crisis induced by nivolumab in a patient with metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of lung.
CASE PRESENTATION
Fifty three-year old woman with metastatic squamous cell carcinoma currently on treatment with nivolumab presented with diffuse facial and tongue swelling, slurred speech, depressed mentation, fatigue and weakness. Initial evaluation revealed severe hypothyroidism with thyroid stimulating hormone of 237 micro Unit/mL (Normal Reference range: 0.27-4.20 micro unit/mL) and undetectable free T4. Patient was diagnosed with nivolumab induced myxedema crisis. She was treated successfully with levothyroxine with complete resolution of her symptoms. Nivolumab was safely restarted once the symptoms of myxedema resolved.
CONCLUSION
Nivolumab can cause immune-mediated endocrinopathies including thyroiditis, hypophysitis, adrenal insufficiency and type 1 diabetes mellitus. High index of suspicion and periodic measurement of thyroid function tests are recommended in patients receiving nivolumab therapy. Our case also suggests that once the myxedema crisis is treated and symptoms are resolved, nivolumab can be safely re-challenged.

data.title: New disappearance of complicated atheromatous plaques on rechallenge with PD-1/PD-L1 axis blockade in non-small cell lung cancer patient: follow up of an unexpected event.
data.abstract: Atherosclerosis is considered an irreversible process, with crucial contribution of inflammation and immune cells. Impact of cancer immunotherapy on a partly immune-driven disease, such as atherosclerosis, is poorly understood, but preclinical models suggest its worsening on programmed death/ligand-1 (PD-1/PD-L1) inhibitors. In a previously reported cohort of 11 patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treated with nivolumab and pre-existing complicated atheromatous plaques, 3 patients had a dramatic radiologic reduction of aortic plaques while on nivolumab; of these 3, 2 died receiving no further treatment. The remaining patient was an 83-year-old woman with history of arterial hypertension and hypothyroidism who was diagnosed with locally advanced squamous NSCLC. At relapse, complicated aortic atheromatous plaques were demonstrated on scans. The patient was then treated with nivolumab obtaining stable disease at radiological assessment, which also demonstrated almost complete vanishing of aortic plaques. After relapse and interval treatment with chemotherapy, she experienced new development of aortic atheromatous plaques. At further relapse she received atezolizumab, which yielded disease response and new reduction in aortic plaques, until nearly complete resolution. The observation of a repeated improvement of atheromatous plaques on treatment with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors favors the protective role of T cells on atheromatous plaques that is impaired by PD-L1 expression by plaque-associated macrophages. Validation by independent and prospective observation is needed.

data.title: Safety and Efficacy of the Rechallenge of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors After Immune-Related Adverse Events in Patients With Cancer: A Systemic Review and Meta-Analysis.
data.abstract:
INTRODUCTION
Little evidence exists on the safety and efficacy of the rechallenge of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) after immune-related adverse events (irAEs) in patients with cancer.
METHODS
We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane for articles on ICI rechallenge after irAEs for systemic review and meta-analysis. The outcomes included the incidence and associated factors for safety and objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) for efficacy.
RESULTS
A total of 789 ICI rechallenge cases from 18 cohort studies, 5 case series studies, and 54 case reports were included. The pooled incidence of all-grade and high-grade irAEs after rechallenge in patients with cancer was 34.2% and 11.7%, respectively. Compared with initial ICI treatment, rechallenge showed a higher incidence for all-grade irAEs (OR, 3.81; 95% CI, 2.15-6.74; p < 0.0001), but similar incidence for high-grade irAEs ( p > 0.05). Types of initial irAEs (pneumonitis and global irAEs) and cancer (non-small cell lung cancer and multiple cancer) recapitulated these findings. Gastrointestinal irAEs and time interval between initial irAEs and ICI rechallenge were associated with higher recurrence of high-grade irAEs ( p < 0.05), whereas initial anti-PD-1/PD-L1 antibodies were associated with a lower recurrence ( p < 0.05). Anti-PD-1/PD-L1 antibodies rechallenge was associated with a lower all-grade irAE recurrence ( p < 0.05). The pooled ORR and DCR after rechallenge were 43.1% and 71.9%, respectively, showing no significant difference compared with initial ICI treatment ( p > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS
ICI rechallenge after irAEs showed lower safety and similar efficacy outcomes compared with initial ICI treatment.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION
PROSPERO, identifier CRD42020191405.

An estimated 40% (95% CI: 30%-51%) of patients of all patients with ICI hepatitis were rechallenged with an ICI, and of those rechallenged, there was an estimated 22% (95% CI: 15%-30%) recurrence.
CONCLUSIONS
Corticosteroids are the primary treatment for ICI hepatitis, with mycophenolate mofetil used as a secondary option for steroids-refractory cases. Current practices mostly rely on expert consensus, highlighting the need for further research to validate and optimize these treatments, particularly for steroid-resistant cases.

data.title: Thrombocytopenia in patients with melanoma receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
data.abstract:
BACKGROUND
Immune checkpoint inhibitors, including antibodies against programmed death 1 (PD-1) and cytotoxic T-lymphocyte antigen 4 (CTLA-4), are being used with increasing frequency for the treatment of cancer. Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) including colitis, dermatitis, and pneumonitis are well described, but less frequent events are now emerging with larger numbers of patients treated. Herein we describe the incidence and spectrum of thrombocytopenia following immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy and two severe cases of idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP).
CASE PRESENTATIONS
A 47-year-old female with recurrent BRAF mutant positive melanoma received combination anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4. Two weeks later, she presented with mucosal bleeding, petechiae, and thrombocytopenia and was treated with standard therapy for ITP with steroids and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Her diagnosis was confirmed with bone marrow biopsy, and given the lack of treatment response, she was treated with rituximab. She began to have recovery and stabilization of her platelet count that ultimately allowed her to be retreated with PD-1 inhibition with no further thrombocytopenia. A second patient, a 45-year-old female with a BRAF wild-type melanoma, received anti-PD-1 monotherapy and became thrombocytopenic 43 days later. Three weeks of steroid treatment improved her platelet count, but thrombocytopenia recurred and required additional steroids. She later received anti-CTLA-4 monotherapy and developed severe ITP with intracranial hemorrhage. Her ITP resolved after treatment of prednisone, IVIG, and rituximab and discontinuation of checkpoint inhibition. In a retrospective chart review of 2360 patients with melanoma treated with checkpoint inhibitor therapy, <1% experienced thrombocytopenia following immune checkpoint inhibition, and of these, most had spontaneous resolution and did not require treatment.
CONCLUSIONS
Thrombocytopenia, especially ITP, induced by immune checkpoint inhibitors appears to be an uncommon irAE that is manageable with observation in mild cases and/or standard ITP treatment algorithms. In our series, the majority of patients had mild thrombocytopenia that resolved spontaneously or responded to standard corticosteroid regimens. However, in two severe cases, IVIG and rituximab, in addition to steroids, were required. Checkpoint inhibition was resumed successfully in the first patient but rechallenge was not tolerated by the second patient.

trajectory.final_answer:
# Bottom line

- There is growing clinical evidence—mainly case reports and small case series—that immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can be rechallenged after immune-related adverse events (irAEs), with successful tumor control in selected patients, but rechallenge carries a higher risk of irAE recurrence, particularly for organ-specific toxicities, and requires careful patient selection and monitoring. <cite id="34646270,35389138,39225744">There is growing clinical evidence—mainly case reports and small case series—that immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can be rechallenged after immune-related adverse events (irAEs), with successful tumor control in selected patients, but rechallenge carries a higher risk of irAE recurrence, particularly for organ-specific toxicities, and requires careful patient selection and monitoring.</cite>

# What supports re-challenge?

- Systematic reviews and meta-analyses have synthesized outcomes across many rechallenge cases. One meta-analysis of 789 rechallenges from 18 cohort and case series studies found that rechallenge was feasible but not without risk, with pooled all-grade and high-grade irAE recurrence rates of 34.2% and 11.7%, respectively, and noted that certain irAE types (e.g., pneumonitis, global irAEs) and tumor types (e.g., NSCLC) were associated with higher recurrence. <cite id="34646270">A meta-analysis of 789 rechallenges from 18 cohort and case series studies found that rechallenge was feasible but not without risk, with pooled all-grade and high-grade irAE recurrence rates of 34.2% and 11.7%, respectively, and noted that certain irAE types (e.g., pneumonitis, global irAEs) and tumor types (e.g., NSCLC) were associated with higher recurrence.</cite>

- Another systematic review reported heterogeneous efficacy across studies, with overall response rates ranging from 0% to 54%, progression-free survival from 1.5 to 12.9 months, and overall survival from 6.5 to 23.8 months, and highlighted that patients with better ECOG performance, longer duration on initial ICI, discontinuation not due to progression, and non-switch sequencing between anti–PD-1 and anti–PD-L1 tended to have better outcomes; importantly, it also emphasized that certain irAEs were more likely to relapse upon retreatment. <cite id="35389138">Another systematic review reported heterogeneous efficacy across studies, with overall response rates ranging from 0% to 54%, progression-free survival from 1.5 to 12.9 months, and overall survival from 6.5 to 23.8 months, and highlighted that patients with better ECOG performance, longer duration on initial ICI, discontinuation not due to progression, and non-switch sequencing between anti–PD-1 and anti–PD-L1 tended to have better outcomes; importantly, it also emphasized that certain irAEs were more likely to relapse upon retreatment.</cite>

- Disease-specific and organ-specific case series provide concrete examples. For endocrine toxicities, case reports describe successful rechallenge after hypothyroidism/myxedema crisis and other endocrinopathies once the acute event resolved, suggesting that targeted management and rechallenge can be undertaken cautiously. <cite id="28239466">Case reports describe successful rechallenge after hypothyroidism/myxedema crisis and other endocrinopathies once the acute event resolved, suggesting that targeted management and rechallenge can be undertaken cautiously.</cite> In contrast, a systematic review of cranial nerve palsy (CNP-ICI) found that rechallenge was significantly associated with the emergence of new irAEs, underscoring that some neurologic irAEs may be less suitable for rechallenge. <cite id="39225744">A systematic review of cranial nerve palsy (CNP-ICI) found that rechallenge was significantly associated with the emergence of new irAEs, underscoring that some neurologic irAEs may be less suitable for rechallenge.</cite>

- Broader retreatment evidence (not strictly rechallenge after prior irAEs but relevant context) shows that switching or reusing ICIs after progression can yield meaningful tumor responses with generally tolerable safety, supporting the biological plausibility of rechallenge when irAEs are managed. For example, in solid tumors, retreatment with anti–PD-(L)1 agents achieved objective response rates of 5–53%, disease control rates of 38–83%, and median overall survival of about 13.9 months, with grade ≥3 irAEs ranging from 0–15% when using a single anti–PD-(L)1 agent. <cite id="33294036">In solid tumors, retreatment with anti–PD-(L)1 agents achieved objective response rates of 5–53%, disease control rates of 38–83%, and median overall survival of about 13.9 months, with grade ≥3 irAEs ranging from 0–15% when using a single anti–PD-(L)1 agent.</cite>

# Recurrence rates of toxicity vs antitumor efficacy upon re-challenge

- Toxicity recurrence: Rechallenge increases the risk of irAEs compared with initial treatment. In a pooled analysis, all-grade irAEs occurred in 34.2% and high-grade irAEs in 11.7% upon rechallenge; importantly, rechallenge showed a higher incidence of all-grade irAEs than initial treatment (OR 3.81, 95% CI 2.15–6.74), while high-grade irAE incidence was similar. Certain organ toxicities (e.g., pneumonitis and gastrointestinal irAEs) and shorter time intervals from initial irAE to rechallenge were associated with higher high-grade irAE recurrence, whereas anti–PD-1/PD-L1 rechallenge was associated with lower all-grade irAE recurrence. <cite id="34646270">In a pooled analysis, all-grade irAEs occurred in 34.2% and high-grade irAEs in 11.7% upon rechallenge; importantly, rechallenge showed a higher incidence of all-grade irAEs than initial treatment (OR 3.81, 95% CI 2.15–6.74), while high-grade irAE incidence was similar. Certain organ toxicities (e.g., pneumonitis and gastrointestinal irAEs) and shorter time intervals from initial irAE to rechallenge were associated with higher high-grade irAE recurrence, whereas anti–PD-1/PD-L1 rechallenge was associated with lower all-grade irAE recurrence.</cite>

- Antitumor efficacy: Efficacy signals upon rechallenge are present but heterogeneous. The pooled objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) after rechallenge were 43.1% and 71.9%, respectively, with no significant difference versus initial ICI treatment in available comparisons. <cite id="34646270">The pooled objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) after rechallenge were 43.1% and 71.9%, respectively, with no significant difference versus initial ICI treatment in available comparisons.</cite> A broader review reported ORRs from 0% to 54%, with progression-free survival ranging from 1.5 to 12.9 months and overall survival from 6.5 to 23.8 months, emphasizing variability by patient and treatment factors. <cite id="35389138">A broader review reported ORRs from 0% to 54%, with progression-free survival ranging from 1.5 to 12.9 months and overall survival from 6.5 to 23.8 months, emphasizing variability by patient and treatment factors.</cite>

- Organ-specific nuances: For endocrine toxicities, case reports describe successful rechallenge after myxedema crisis and other thyroid events once acute symptoms resolved, suggesting that with careful management, antitumor benefit can be pursued. <cite id="28239466">Case reports describe successful rechallenge after myxedema crisis and other thyroid events once acute symptoms resolved, suggesting that with careful management, antitumor benefit can be pursued.</cite> For cranial nerve palsy, rechallenge was associated with new irAEs and poorer recovery profiles, indicating that neurologic irAEs may be less favorable for rechallenge. <cite id="39225744">For cranial nerve palsy, rechallenge was associated with new irAEs and poorer recovery profiles, indicating that neurologic irAEs may be less favorable for rechallenge.</cite>

# Practical considerations and patient selection

- Rechallenge appears feasible and sometimes beneficial for selected patients, particularly when irAEs are steroid-responsive and not organ-limiting, and when careful monitoring and risk mitigation are in place. <cite id="35389138">Rechallenge appears feasible and sometimes beneficial for selected patients, particularly when irAEs are steroid-responsive and not organ-limiting, and when careful monitoring and risk mitigation are in place.</cite> Evidence suggests that anti–PD-1/PD-L1 rechallenge may carry a lower risk of overall irAE recurrence compared with CTLA-4–related rechallenge, and that longer time intervals from initial irAE to rechallenge may reduce high-grade toxicity recurrence. <cite id="34646270">Evidence suggests that anti–PD-1/PD-L1 rechallenge may carry a lower risk of overall irAE recurrence compared with CTLA-4–related rechallenge, and that longer time intervals from initial irAE to rechallenge may reduce high-grade toxicity recurrence.</cite>

- Specialized toxicities require caution. For example, in steroid-refractory ICI hepatitis, rechallenge after immunosuppression is practiced, with an estimated 40% of patients rechallenged and about 22% recurrence of hepatitis upon rechallenge in pooled data. <cite id="39298568">In steroid-refractory ICI hepatitis, rechallenge after immunosuppression is practiced, with an estimated 40% of patients rechallenged and about 22% recurrence of hepatitis upon rechallenge in pooled data.</cite> Some case series show that rechallenge can be tolerated and lead to disease control in specific hematologic or endocrine toxicities, but severe or steroid-refractory cases may not tolerate rechallenge. <cite id="28239462">Some case series show that rechallenge can be tolerated and lead to disease control in specific hematologic or endocrine toxicities, but severe or steroid-refractory cases may not tolerate rechallenge.</cite>

# Conclusion

- The evidence base for rechallenge after prior irAEs is strongest for endocrine toxicities and certain pneumonitis/colitis cases, with supportive cohort and case series data showing meaningful tumor responses but higher-than-initial-treatment toxicity recurrence rates. <cite id="34646270,35389138,28239466">The evidence base for rechallenge after prior irAEs is strongest for endocrine toxicities and certain pneumonitis/colitis cases, with supportive cohort and case series data showing meaningful tumor responses but higher-than-initial-treatment toxicity recurrence rates.</cite> Neurologic irAEs such as cranial nerve palsies appear less favorable for rechallenge due to higher risk of new or recurrent toxicity. <cite id="39225744">Neurologic irAEs such as cranial nerve palsies appear less favorable for rechallenge due to higher risk of new or recurrent toxicity.</cite> Overall, rechallenge can be considered in selected patients with careful multidisciplinary evaluation, close monitoring, and individualized risk–benefit assessment, recognizing that while antitumor efficacy is achievable, toxicity recurrence is more likely than with initial therapy. <cite id="34646270,35389138">Overall, rechallenge can be considered in selected patients with careful multidisciplinary evaluation, close monitoring, and individualized risk–benefit assessment, recognizing that while antitumor efficacy is achievable, toxicity recurrence is more likely than with initial therapy.</cite>

<snippet id="24433497">Title: The M50I polymorphic substitution in association with the R263K mutation in HIV-1 subtype B integrase increases drug resistance but does not restore viral replicative fitness.
Authors: Wares, Melissa, Mesplède, Thibault, Quashie, Peter K et al. | Year: 2014 | Journal: Retrovirology
Abstract: BACKGROUND
First-generation integrase strand-transfer inhibitors (INSTIs), such as raltegravir (RAL) and elvitegravir (EVG), have been clinically proven to be effective antiretrovirals for the treatment of HIV-positive patients. However, their relatively low genetic barrier for resistance makes them susceptible to the emergence of drug resistance mutations. In contrast, dolutegravir (DTG) is a newer INSTI that appears to have a high genetic barrier to resistance in vivo. However, the emergence of the resistance mutation R263K followed by the polymorphic substitution M50I has been observed in cell culture. The M50I polymorphism is also observed in 10-25% of INSTI-naïve patients and has been reported in combination with R263K in a patient failing treatment with RAL.
RESULTS
Using biochemical cell-free strand-transfer assays and resistance assays in TZM-bl cells, we demonstrate that the M50I polymorphism in combination with R263K increases resistance to DTG in tissue culture and in biochemical assays but does not restore the viral fitness cost associated with the R263K mutation.
CONCLUSIONS
Since the combination of the R263K mutation and the M50I polymorphism results in a virus with decreased viral fitness and limited cross-resistance, the R263K resistance pathway may represent an evolutionary dead-end. Although this hypothesis has not yet been proven, it may be more advantageous to treat HIV-positive individuals with DTG in first-line than in second or third-line therapy.</snippet>
<snippet id="23529738">Title: Impact of primary elvitegravir resistance-associated mutations in HIV-1 integrase on drug susceptibility and viral replication fitness.
Authors: Abram, Michael E, Hluhanich, Rebecca M, Goodman, Derrick D et al. | Year: 2013 | Journal: Antimicrobial agents and chemotherapy
Abstract: Elvitegravir (EVG) is an effective HIV-1 integrase (IN) strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) in advanced clinical development. Primary INSTI resistance-associated mutations (RAMs) at six IN positions have been identified in HIV-1-infected patients failing EVG-containing regimens in clinical studies: T66I/A/K, E92Q/G, T97A, S147G, Q148R/H/K, and N155H. In this study, the effect of these primary IN mutations, alone and in combination, on susceptibility to the INSTIs EVG, raltegravir (RAL), and dolutegravir (DTG); IN enzyme activities; and viral replication fitness was characterized. Recombinant viruses containing the six most common mutations exhibited a range of reduced EVG susceptibility: 92-fold for Q148R, 30-fold for N155H, 26-fold for E92Q, 10-fold for T66I, 4-fold for S147G, and 2-fold for T97A. Less commonly observed primary IN mutations also showed a range of reduced EVG susceptibilities: 40- to 94-fold for T66K and Q148K and 5- to 10-fold for T66A, E92G, and Q148H. Some primary IN mutations exhibited broad cross-resistance between EVG and RAL (T66K, E92Q, Q148R/H/K, and N155H), while others retained susceptibility to RAL (T66I/A, E92G, T97A, and S147G). Dual combinations of primary IN mutations further reduced INSTI susceptibility, replication capacity, and viral fitness relative to either mutation alone. Susceptibility to DTG was retained by single primary IN mutations but reduced by dual mutation combinations with Q148R. Primary EVG RAMs also diminished IN enzymatic activities, concordant with their structural proximity to the active site. Greater reductions in viral fitness of dual mutation combinations may explain why some primary INSTI RAMs do not readily coexist on the same HIV-1 genome but rather establish independent pathways of resistance to EVG.</snippet>
<snippet id="15577623">Title: Multiple mutations in human immunodeficiency virus-1 integrase confer resistance to the clinical trial drug S-1360.
Authors: Fikkert, Valery, Hombrouck, Anneleen, Van Remoortel, Barbara et al. | Year: 2004 | Journal: AIDS (London, England)
Abstract: OBJECTIVES
Study of HIV-1 resistance development to the diketo analogue S-1360, the first HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor that has entered clinical development.
DESIGN
HIV-1(IIIB) was passaged in cell culture in the presence of increasing concentrations of S-1360 (IIIB/S-1360(res)).
METHODS
The IIIB/S-1360(res) strains selected for 30, 50 and 70 passages in the presence of S-1360 were evaluated genotypically by sequencing analysis and phenotypically using the MT-4/MTT assay.
RESULTS
Multiple mutations, nine in total, emerged progressively in the catalytic domain of integrase as a result of the selection process. They included T66I and L74M that have both been associated with resistance against the diketo acid L-708,906. After 30, 50 and 70 passages in the presence of S-1360, IIIB/S-1360(res) displayed a four-, eight- and more than 62-fold reduced susceptibility for S-1360, respectively. Phenotypic cross-resistance to L-708,906 was modest for the IIIB/S-1360(res) strain selected during 50 passages, but pronounced for the strain selected during 70 passages. Interesting, all IIIB/S-1360(res) strains remained fully susceptible to the pyranodipyrimidine V-165, an integrase DNA binding inhibitor. Recombination of the mutant integrase genes into wild-type background by integrase-chimeric virus technology entirely reproduced the resistance profile of the IIIB/S-1360(res) strains. As for the replication kinetics of the selected and recombined strains, reduced replication fitness was measured for all strains when compared with their respective wild-type strains.
CONCLUSIONS
The accumulation of integrase mutations coincided with an increasing level of (cross-)resistance of IIIB/S-1360(res). Integrase-chimeric virus technology confirmed that the integrase mutations are indeed fully responsible for the resistance phenotype of IIIB/S-1360.</snippet>

<answer>
# Summary

Integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) resistance mutations in HIV-1 commonly reduce viral replicative fitness while conferring variable degrees of cross-resistance to other INSTIs. Single mutations such as Q148R or N155H can produce large fold-changes in reduced susceptibility to elvitegravir (EVG) and sometimes retain susceptibility to raltegravir (RAL), whereas other mutations like T66K/E92Q can show broader cross-resistance across multiple INSTIs. Fitness costs often increase when resistance mutations co-occur, and certain compensatory polymorphisms (e.g., M50I) may enhance resistance without restoring fitness, suggesting evolutionary dead-ends in specific resistance pathways. The emergence of cross-resistance patterns is linked to the structural and functional proximity of mutations to the integrase active site and DNA-binding domains, and newer INSTIs (e.g., dolutegravir, DTG) generally maintain activity against earlier resistance mutations but can lose potency with specific double mutations (e.g., Q148R plus others).

# Effects on Viral Fitness

- Single primary EVG resistance-associated mutations (RAMs) reduce viral replication capacity relative to wild-type virus, with the magnitude of fitness loss correlating with the degree of reduced EVG susceptibility. Q148R and N155H produce the largest fitness costs, while some mutations (e.g., T66I/A, E92G, T97A, S147G) retain RAL susceptibility and less severe fitness defects. Dual combinations of primary mutations further reduce replication capacity and fitness compared to single mutations, helping explain why multiple resistance pathways often arise rather than large composite resistance mutations coexisting on the same genome. <cite id="23529738">Single primary integrase mutations reduce replication capacity and fitness, with dual combinations causing greater reductions; some mutations retain RAL susceptibility while others show broad cross-resistance to EVG and reduced RAL susceptibility</cite>.

- The M50I polymorphism, frequently observed in INSTI-naïve individuals, increases resistance to dolutegravir (DTG) when combined with R263K but does not restore the replicative fitness deficit imposed by R263K, leading to overall decreased viral fitness and limited cross-resistance; this suggests the R263K→M50I pathway may be an evolutionary dead-end. <cite id="24433497">The M50I polymorphism with R263K increases DTG resistance but does not restore fitness, resulting in decreased viral fitness and limited cross-resistance, suggesting an evolutionary dead-end</cite>.

- Early diketo-acid integrase inhibitors (e.g., L-708,906) showed that resistance mutations (e.g., T66I, L74M) confer modest cross-resistance to related compounds but retain susceptibility to other INSTI classes such as pyranodipyrimidines (e.g., V-1653). Accumulation of multiple integrase mutations progressively increases resistance but reduces replication fitness compared to wild-type virus. <cite id="15577623">Resistance to diketo integrase inhibitors selects mutations (e.g., T66I, L74M) with modest cross-resistance to L-708,906 and full susceptibility to V-1653; replication fitness is reduced in resistant strains</cite>.

# Cross-Resistance Patterns Across INSTIs

- Broad cross-resistance between EVG and RAL occurs with certain primary RAMs: T66K, E92Q, Q148R/H/K, and N155H, whereas other mutations (T66I/A, E92G, T97A, S147G) largely retain RAL susceptibility. <cite id="23529738">Mutations T66K, E92Q, Q148R/H/K, and N155H show broad cross-resistance between EVG and RAL, while T66I/A, E92G, T97A, and S147G retain RAL susceptibility</cite>.

data.title: The M50I polymorphic substitution in association with the R263K mutation in HIV-1 subtype B integrase increases drug resistance but does not restore viral replicative fitness.
data.abstract:
BACKGROUND
First-generation integrase strand-transfer inhibitors (INSTIs), such as raltegravir (RAL) and elvitegravir (EVG), have been clinically proven to be effective antiretrovirals for the treatment of HIV-positive patients. However, their relatively low genetic barrier for resistance makes them susceptible to the emergence of drug resistance mutations. In contrast, dolutegravir (DTG) is a newer INSTI that appears to have a high genetic barrier to resistance in vivo. However, the emergence of the resistance mutation R263K followed by the polymorphic substitution M50I has been observed in cell culture. The M50I polymorphism is also observed in 10-25% of INSTI-naïve patients and has been reported in combination with R263K in a patient failing treatment with RAL.
RESULTS
Using biochemical cell-free strand-transfer assays and resistance assays in TZM-bl cells, we demonstrate that the M50I polymorphism in combination with R263K increases resistance to DTG in tissue culture and in biochemical assays but does not restore the viral fitness cost associated with the R263K mutation.
CONCLUSIONS
Since the combination of the R263K mutation and the M50I polymorphism results in a virus with decreased viral fitness and limited cross-resistance, the R263K resistance pathway may represent an evolutionary dead-end. Although this hypothesis has not yet been proven, it may be more advantageous to treat HIV-positive individuals with DTG in first-line than in second or third-line therapy.

data.title: Impact of primary elvitegravir resistance-associated mutations in HIV-1 integrase on drug susceptibility and viral replication fitness.
data.abstract: Elvitegravir (EVG) is an effective HIV-1 integrase (IN) strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) in advanced clinical development. Primary INSTI resistance-associated mutations (RAMs) at six IN positions have been identified in HIV-1-infected patients failing EVG-containing regimens in clinical studies: T66I/A/K, E92Q/G, T97A, S147G, Q148R/H/K, and N155H. In this study, the effect of these primary IN mutations, alone and in combination, on susceptibility to the INSTIs EVG, raltegravir (RAL), and dolutegravir (DTG); IN enzyme activities; and viral replication fitness was characterized. Recombinant viruses containing the six most common mutations exhibited a range of reduced EVG susceptibility: 92-fold for Q148R, 30-fold for N155H, 26-fold for E92Q, 10-fold for T66I, 4-fold for S147G, and 2-fold for T97A. Less commonly observed primary IN mutations also showed a range of reduced EVG susceptibilities: 40- to 94-fold for T66K and Q148K and 5- to 10-fold for T66A, E92G, and Q148H. Some primary IN mutations exhibited broad cross-resistance between EVG and RAL (T66K, E92Q, Q148R/H/K, and N155H), while others retained susceptibility to RAL (T66I/A, E92G, T97A, and S147G). Dual combinations of primary IN mutations further reduced INSTI susceptibility, replication capacity, and viral fitness relative to either mutation alone. Susceptibility to DTG was retained by single primary IN mutations but reduced by dual mutation combinations with Q148R. Primary EVG RAMs also diminished IN enzymatic activities, concordant with their structural proximity to the active site. Greater reductions in viral fitness of dual mutation combinations may explain why some primary INSTI RAMs do not readily coexist on the same HIV-1 genome but rather establish independent pathways of resistance to EVG.

data.title: Multiple mutations in human immunodeficiency virus-1 integrase confer resistance to the clinical trial drug S-1360.
data.abstract:
OBJECTIVES
Study of HIV-1 resistance development to the diketo analogue S-1360, the first HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor that has entered clinical development.
DESIGN
HIV-1(IIIB) was passaged in cell culture in the presence of increasing concentrations of S-1360 (IIIB/S-1360(res)).
METHODS
The IIIB/S-1360(res) strains selected for 30, 50 and 70 passages in the presence of S-1360 were evaluated genotypically by sequencing analysis and phenotypically using the MT-4/MTT assay.
RESULTS
Multiple mutations, nine in total, emerged progressively in the catalytic domain of integrase as a result of the selection process. They included T66I and L74M that have both been associated with resistance against the diketo acid L-708,906. After 30, 50 and 70 passages in the presence of S-1360, IIIB/S-1360(res) displayed a four-, eight- and more than 62-fold reduced susceptibility for S-1360, respectively. Phenotypic cross-resistance to L-708,906 was modest for the IIIB/S-1360(res) strain selected during 50 passages, but pronounced for the strain selected during 70 passages. Interesting, all IIIB/S-1360(res) strains remained fully susceptible to the pyranodipyrimidine V-165, an integrase DNA binding inhibitor. Recombination of the mutant integrase genes into wild-type background by integrase-chimeric virus technology entirely reproduced the resistance profile of the IIIB/S-1360(res) strains. As for the replication kinetics of the selected and recombined strains, reduced replication fitness was measured for all strains when compared with their respective wild-type strains.
CONCLUSIONS
The accumulation of integrase mutations coincided with an increasing level of (cross-)resistance of IIIB/S-1360(res). Integrase-chimeric virus technology confirmed that the integrase mutations are indeed fully responsible for the resistance phenotype of IIIB/S-1360.

<snippet id="38092229">Title: Trastuzumab deruxtecan in previously treated patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer: updated survival results from a phase II trial (DESTINY-Breast01).
Authors: Saura, C, Modi, S, Krop, I et al. | Year: 2024 | Journal: Annals of oncology : official journal of the European Society for Medical Oncology
Abstract: BACKGROUND
Primary analysis of the multicenter, open-label, single-arm, phase II DESTINY-Breast01 trial (median follow-up 11.1 months) demonstrated durable antitumor activity with trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) in patients with human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive metastatic breast cancer (mBC) previously treated with trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1). We report updated cumulative survival outcomes with a median follow-up of 26.5 months (data cut-off 26 March 2021).
PATIENTS AND METHODS
Patients with HER2-positive mBC resistant or refractory to T-DM1 received T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks until disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, or withdrawal of consent. The primary endpoint was confirmed objective response rate (ORR) by independent central review (ICR). Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), duration of response (DoR), progression-free survival (PFS), and safety.
RESULTS
The ORR by ICR was 62.0% [95% confidence interval (CI) 54.5% to 69.0%] in patients who received T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg every 3 weeks (n = 184). Median OS was 29.1 months (95% CI 24.6-36.1 months). Median PFS and DoR were 19.4 months (95% CI 14.1-25.0 months) and 18.2 months (95% CI 15.0 months-not evaluable), respectively. Drug-related treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were observed in 183 patients (99.5%), and 99 patients (53.8%) had one or more grade ≥3 TEAEs. Adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis occurred in 15.8% of patients (n = 29), of which 2.7% (n = 5) were grade 5.
CONCLUSIONS
These updated results provide further evidence of sustained antitumor activity of T-DXd with a consistent safety profile in heavily pretreated patients with HER2-positive mBC.</snippet>

<snippet id="23020162">Title: Trastuzumab emtansine for HER2-positive advanced breast cancer.
Authors: Verma, Sunil, Miles, David, Gianni, Luca et al. | Year: 2012 | Journal: The New England journal of medicine
Abstract: BACKGROUND
Trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) is an antibody-drug conjugate incorporating the human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-targeted antitumor properties of trastuzumab with the cytotoxic activity of the microtubule-inhibitory agent DM1. The antibody and the cytotoxic agent are conjugated by means of a stable linker.
METHODS
We randomly assigned patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer, who had previously been treated with trastuzumab and a taxane, to T-DM1 or lapatinib plus capecitabine. The primary end points were progression-free survival (as assessed by independent review), overall survival, and safety. Secondary end points included progression-free survival (investigator-assessed), the objective response rate, and the time to symptom progression. Two interim analyses of overall survival were conducted.
RESULTS
Among 991 randomly assigned patients, median progression-free survival as assessed by independent review was 9.6 months with T-DM1 versus 6.4 months with lapatinib plus capecitabine (hazard ratio for progression or death from any cause, 0.65; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.55 to 0.77; P<0.001), and median overall survival at the second interim analysis crossed the stopping boundary for efficacy (30.9 months vs. 25.1 months; hazard ratio for death from any cause, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.85; P<0.001). The objective response rate was higher with T-DM1 (43.6%, vs. 30.8% with lapatinib plus capecitabine; P<0.001); results for all additional secondary end points favored T-DM1. Rates of grade 3 or 4 adverse events were higher with lapatinib plus capecitabine than with T-DM1 (57% vs. 41%). The incidences of thrombocytopenia and increased serum aminotransferase levels were higher with T-DM1, whereas the incidences of diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia were higher with lapatinib plus capecitabine.
CONCLUSIONS
T-DM1 significantly prolonged progression-free and overall survival with less toxicity than lapatinib plus capecitabine in patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane. (Funded by F. Hoffmann-La Roche/Genentech; EMILIA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00829166.).</snippet>
